Commentary.Commentary: England will not to be too happy with the final total after electing to bat. The conditions were tough and apart from Root and Stokes, none of the other batsmen showed the desire to weather the storm. Had West Indies not dropped so many catches, things would have been even worse for them. Now the onus is on their bowlers to perform on a pitch which has a plenty of juice. Let's see how West Indies respond...

Great bowling effort by the Windies! Kemar Roach and Shannon Gabriel delivered the goods on a pitch which is providing a lot of assistance to the seamers. Both the pacers bagging four wickets each, helping the visitors to bowl out the hosts for a moderate total.

OUT! So they wrap up things quickly. Roach gets his fourth. He serves a short delivery outside off, Woakes tries to work it down to third man but gets an outside edge to Dowrich who makes no mistake this time. ENGLAND HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 258!
Fuller on off, Woakes drives it to mid off.
Tad shorter outside off, Woakes tries to guide it down to third man but gets a bottom edge.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Good length outside off, Woakes lets it through to the keeper.
Lands it on a length outside off, Anderson allows it through to the keeper. A double-wicket maiden!
James Anderson is the last batsman.
OUT! Boom, right through the gate! Gabriel does it all by himself. Hurls across a toe-crushing yorker, right in the blockhole, too quick for Broad to dig it out and it goes on to rattle the stumps.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

DROPPED AGAIN! How many more are the West Indian players going to drop? Length ball on off angling away, Broad tries to defend but gets an outside edge straight to the keeper who drops a sitter. Poor by the keeper that should have been gobbled. Gabriel cannot believe it.
Stuart Broad the new man in, receives a short ball on off, he does well to defend it off the back foot.

OUT! They finally hang onto one. The bowling change has worked again. Gabriel who dropped him earlier has got his man. He bangs it short on middle, Stokes goes for the pull but it takes the edge and goes to the keeper who takes a good catch going to his left. The players appeal and Ben starts walking. He gets a sendoff from Shannon on his way but a brilliant innings from him nonetheless. He walks off to a standing ovation from the crowd. Has done his part. England are 8 down now. Can they get to 300?
Shannon Gabriel gets back into the attack, the captain finally realizes that Roston Chase is not doing a good job, chuckles Michael Holding on-air.

Edged but short! Who wants to be Kemar Roach? I surely don't want to be in his place. Nothing going his way. Another edge induced but it has fallen short of first slip. A speechless Roach takes his cap and walks away. Not your day, mate!
FOUR! What an asset to have batting at number 9! Short delivery angling into the batsman, Woakes swivels and helps his pull shot over backward square leg for a boundary.
Shortish and wide outside off, Woakes cuts it straight to point.
Angling into the batsman, Woakes stands back in defense.
A little bit of room outside off, Woakes plays it down with an angled bat and it goes off the outer half to gully, on one bounce though.
Fuller in length on off, driven off the front foot to mid off.
Drinks break.
Plays it with the angle towards mid-wicket for a run.

Michael Holding is furious with Jason Holder's tactics. He makes a valid point that the main spinner, Devendra Bishoo has just bowled six overs today while the part-timer Roston Chase keeps on bowling in spite of being expensive. Fair point. Hard to understand this ploy!
Drags his length back outside off, Woakes gets it past the slip fielder and the ball races away.
Floats it on off, Woakes drives it back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries. Shorter outside off, Woakes plays it through short third man for a boundary.
FOUR! Fires it down the leg side, Woakes tickles it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
6th Test hundred for Ben Stokes.

HUNDRED FOR STOKES! He has been dropped twice, but take nothing away form this knock. Brilliant attacking display by him. Roach lands it on a length outside off, Stokes drives it through covers and runs two. He is all smiles as he raises his bat. Top knock from a top batsman!

DROPPED! Stokes has another reprieve. You could see this coming, he was getting a bit fidgety. Roach bowls a fuller ball on off, Stokes walks down the track and tries to club it over mid on but hits it straight to Gabriel who is stationed there. Shannon gets two hands to it but can't hold onto it. Ben Stokes will breathe a sigh of a relief. Kemar stands a frustrated figure. You have to feel for him as he has bowled his heart out and not gotten support from his fielders.
Almost an edge there. Bowls it full and wide outside off, Stokes goes after it but does not connect.
Length outside off, Stokes goes hard at it but hits it straight to the man at covers.
Lands it on a length outside off, comes back into the batsman. Stokes watchfully lets it through to the keeper.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Sprays on the pads, Woakes tries to flick it but misses as the ball brushes the pads and it goes down to fine leg for two leg byes.
Bowls an arm ball on off, Stokes pushes it through covers for a run.
Fires it on off, Stokes lunges forward and defends it.
Bowls it outside off, Stokes opts to not play at it.
Flatter on off, turning away. Stokes defends it watchfully.
Back of a length outside off, Woakes lets it be.
A tad short outside off, Stokes cuts it to deep point to change strike.
Fuller ball outside off, Stokes eases it straight to covers. He would feel he missed out there. That was right in his arc.
On the shorter side on off, Stokes pushes it to mid off.
Bangs in a short one on middle, Stokes plays a short-arm jab through mid-wicket and the batsmen run two. A boundary away now.
Back of a length on off, angling across the batsman. Stokes pushes it back to the bowler.
Floats it on middle, Woakes flicks it uppishly towards mid on.
Loopy ball on off, Woakes drives it to mid off.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
FOUR! Poor from Chase. Fast hands from Chris Woakes. Drags his length back outside off, Woakes goes back and waits for the ball as he cuts it late past the backward point fielder and into the fence.
Flatter outside off, the batsman opts not to play at it.
Tosses it up on off, Woakes works it with the spin to mid on.
Lands it on a length, angling across the batsman. Stokes lets it through to the keeper.
Bowls it from over the wicket on the pads, Stokes flicks it behind square on the leg side for a couple. He moves onto 94 here. One hit away.
FOUR! We are running out of superlatives for how this guy is playing. What a shot! Full ball outside off, Stokes shuffles across early and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
A tad fuller outside off, Stokes drives it to covers.
Fuller in length this time on off, Stokes eases his drive to mid off.
Back of a length from around the wicket on off, Stokes with his high bat lift defends it off the back foot.
Floats it on off, Woakes prods forward and defends it.
Plays it with the spin to mid-wicket.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy ball on off, Chris drives it to covers who does well to stop it.
LOVELY BOWLING! Flights it on off, Woakes plays for the turn but the ball straightens and beats the outside edge.
Fires it on off, gets some extra bounce. Stokes hits it down to long on for a run.
Fuller on off, Woakes gets it off the outer half through cover-point for a brace.
Bangs in a well-directed short ball. Woakes does well to evade it.
Bowls a yorker on off, Woakes does well to dig it out.
Lands it on a length outside off, Woakes lets it through to the keeper.
Chris Woakes strides out to the middle. England bat too deep.

OUT! The bowling change has worked wonders. This is exactly the way Moeen Ali got out against South Africa recently. Fuller ball outside off, Moeen drives it but fails to keep it down and it goes straight to Roston Chase at point who takes a nice catch. Kemar provides a crucial breakthrough as this stand was looking dangerous. Can they wrap up things quickly now?
Fuller outside off, Moeen times it to covers.
Kemar Roach is back into the attack. The Windies are in a desperate need of a wicket here.
Tosses it up outside off, Ali drives it through covers for a run.
FOUR! Picked the length very early there! Quicker and shorter on off, Moeen Ali rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Runs coming thick and fast here.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Drags his length back on off, Moeen pushes it to covers.
Floats it outside off, Ali drives it straight to the man at covers.
Flatter outside off, Ali lets it be.
FOUR! Easy for Stokes! On the shorter side on leg stump, Stokes swivels inside his crease and pulls it behind backward square leg for a boundary. He moves onto 87.
Lands it on a length on middle, Stokes defends it by getting behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! The tourists are losing their grip here. Fuller outside off, Stokes leans into it and drives it through covers. This is also Ben Stokes' highest score against the West Indies.
Full on the pads, Stokes clips it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Fullish length on middle, Stokes eases it to mid on. That was beautifully timed but for no runs.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Plays it with the spin through covers for a run.
Tucks it with the angle on the leg side for a run.
FOUR! Through the off side this time. Flighted ball on off, Moeen Ali goes over the head of the mid off fielder for a boundary.
Floats it on off, Ali defends it watchfully.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
FOUR! Moeen is into the action now. Chase Tosses it up on middle, Ali goes over mid-wicket and it goes one bounce into the fence.
Bangs in a short ball on leg stump. Ali tries to go for the pull but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball rolls towards the leg side and the batsmen take a quick run.
A tad fuller on off, Stokes works it towards mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! TOP SHOT! It was not such a bad delivery but Stokes made great use of his wrists there. Fuller on off, Ben flicks it through mid-wicket and the ball races away.
Bowls it outside off, wanting the batsman to slash at it but Stokes opts not to play at it.
Shorter outside off, Stokes tries to cut but is beaten by the low bounce.
Bowls it very wide outside off, Holder shoulders his arms to it.
Floats it on off, Ali defends it off the front foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Drags his length back outside off, Stokes punches it through the off side for a run.

How has that missed the stumps? Stokes is riding his luck. Bowls it on off, turning away. Stokes tries to defend it but gets an inside edge that goes just past the leg stump and down towards fine leg. Blackwood from slip hares after it and keeps it down to two.
Tosses it up on off, Stokes lunges forward and defends it.
Flatter on off, Stokes defends it off the back foot.
A low full toss outside off, Moeen tries to drive but ends up slicing it to gully.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
An inswinger to Moeen first up. On a length on off, Ali gets an inside edge onto his pads. That was a terrific delivery by Holder.
There is now a second slip in place for Ali.
Bangs it in short on middle, Stokes pulls it straight to the man at deep square leg for a run.
Length outside off, Stokes lets it through to the keeper.
Lovely bowling! Lands it on a length, moving away from the batsman. Stokes pokes at it and gets beaten.
Floats it on off, Ben drives it down to long off for a run.
FOUR! Stokes is on the charge here. Plays the paddle sweep fine down the leg side and the ball races to the fence.
Fires it in on off, Ben pushes it off the back foot.
Flatter on off, Stokes punches it to covers.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

TWO BYES! That one has turned sharply! Chase tosses it up outside off, Stokes goes for the expansive drive but the ball turns and beats the edge. It goes past the keeper and the first slip fielder down to third man. The latter gives it a chase and keeps it down to two byes.
Roston Chase comes back into the attack.
Just ahead of a length on the pads, Stokes flicks it to fine leg for a run.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Lands it on a length on off, Stokes pokes at it and gets an outside edge through the slip cordon for a couple.
FOUR! Too easy! Shorter on off, sits up and asking to be hit. Stokes camps back and pulls it through mid-wicket and the ball races to the fence.
Bowls it wide outside off, Ben lets it be.
Lands it on a length outside off, Stokes shoulders his arms to it.
FOUR! On a length outside off, Ali drives it on the up through the cover region and the ball races to the boundary.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Fullish length on middle, Ben gets it off the inner half through mid-wicket for a run.

FOUR! WOW! Shot of the day! Full ball on middle, Stokes just times it straight past the bowler showing the full face of the bat for a boundary. He also holds his pose after playing the shot, top class.
Lands it on a length outside off, Stokes shoulders his arms to it.

FOUR! He has slapped that! A full ball outside off, Stokes goes down on one knee and slaps it through covers for a boundary. That was right in his arc. A gift for him to get to his 11th Test fifty. He still has a long way to go.
Shannon Gabriel will bowl from the other end.
Shorter outside off, Stokes guides it to deep point for a run.

An inswinger on middle, Stokes times his flick towards mid on and sets off for a run. Shannon Gabriel, the big man does well to get down to his left to make a good stop and this effort also stops the batsmen from taking a run.
Walks down the track and Stokes eases the full ball on off to mid off.
A tad fuller outside off, Stokes lets it be.
Lands it on a length outside off, Stokes shoulders his arms to it.
Bangs it in short and wide outside off, Holder chops it on the off side.

NO BALL! He started off with one in the previous session and starts off with one again. Back of a length on off, Stokes tries to defend it but gets an inside edge onto his pads. Holder has overstepped again and the umpire signals a no ball.

We're back for the third session. The players and the umpires are out in the middle. Ben Stokes and Moeen Ali will continue their innings. Jason Holder will start the proceedings after the break for the Windies.
...Day 1, Session 3...

The Englishmen still have some batting to come and they will look to add as many runs as possible to the total. The tourists would want to pick the remaining wickets quickly and restrict the English side under 200, if possible. Join us in a while for the third and the final session.

24 overs, 95 runs and three wickets. This session swung like a pendulum. The Windies started off really well after picking the wicket of Dawid Malan but the free-flowing partnership between Stokes and Root helped shift the momentum back towards the hosts. A lapse in concentration and a false shot by the latter led to his downfall and then the wicket of Bairstow tilted the momentum towards the visitors.
Full on leg stump, Ali flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple. TEA ON DAY 1!
Bowls a well-directed bouncer. Moeen Ali does well to duck under it.
Yorker on middle, Ali does well to dig it out.
Good length, angling across the batsman. Ali tries to poke it but gets beaten.
Lands it on a length on middle, Ali works it to mid-wicket from the crease.

In the air... but safe! Stokes will continue playing his shots. Shannon bangs it in short on middle, Ben takes on the challenge to pull but the ball gets big on him. He gets a top edge which goes over the slip cordon. Jason Holder from second slip gives it a chase but is unable to reach there. The batsmen complete a run.
Flighted on off, Ali lunges forward and defends it.
Fires it on middle, Ali defends it off the back foot.
Flatter outside off, Ali lets it be.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Slower through the air outside off, turning away. Moeen lets it through to the keeper.
Tosses it up on off, Ali drives it to covers.
Roston Chase is brought back into the attack.
Fuller and outside off, Stokes drives it to covers.
Sprays on the pads, Moeen Ali works it around the corner for a run.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Length outside off, the batsman shoulders his arms to it.
Moeen Ali is the next man in.

OUT! A puzzled Jonny Bairstow is walking back. He does not like it, neither does the crowd as they both felt that the ball had hit the ground. Shannon bowls it on a length around off, seaming away from the batsman. Bairstow tries to play at it with firm hands but gets an outside edge to Jason Holder at second slip who takes a good low catch and appeals. Jonny stands his ground as he feels the catch is not clean. After a chat, the umpires go upstairs and replays show that there is not enough evidence to overturn the soft signal which was out. It's touch and go, and Jonny has to go. Gabriel gets his second and this is yet another big wicket for the Windies.
The umpires are going upstairs to check whether Jason Holder has taken the catch cleanly at second slip. The soft signal is out. Holder looks quite confident. Let's see...
Back of a length outside off, Bairstow chops it to point.
Slower through the air around off, stays low a touch. Stokes camps back and tries to force it on the off side but gets an inside edge onto his pads.

A good observation being made by Sir Ian Botham on-air. He feels that Jason Holder has been a reactive captain so far. Brings out the instance of Kemar Roach's spell where he induced an outside edge off Stokes' bat but the catch was dropped. After that a boundary was hit and Holder just followed the ball. As a result, there was one less fielder in the slip cordon through which another edge went for a boundary. Fair point, Beefy. You cannot be restless as a captain. Patience is the mother of all virtues!
Drags his length back outside off, Bairstow cuts it through the cover region for a run.
Flighted ball on off, Jonny lunges forward and defends it.
Floats it on off, Bairstow drives it beautifully to covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tosses it up on middle, Jonny drives it to mid on.
Change of ends for Devendra Bishoo.
Good length on off, jagging back in. Stokes tries to defend it but gets hit on the pads. There is a stifled appeal from the Windies but nothing from the umpire.
FOUR! Poor length! Short and outside off, Stokes cuts it through point and the ball races to the fence. Any width on offer and Stokes will go after it.
Fuller this time around off, Stokes drives it to mid on.
Back of a length on off, Stokes gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
OUCH! That must have hurt! Good length on leg stump, Stokes misses the flick and gets hit on the thigh. He goes down holding that part but he is a strong man and will continue playing.
A tad shorter on leg stump, Bairstow tucks it towards square leg for a run.
Shannon Gabriel is back into the attack.
Fuller outside off, Stokes drives it square on the off side for two.
Lands it on a length outside off, Ben opts not to play at it.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.

FOUR! Shorter in length outside off, Stokes sees the width and cuts it uppishly past the diving gully fielder for a boundary. The fielder there could have done better to prevent the ball from going to the fence.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Lands it on a length outside off, Stokes shoulders his arms to it.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Jonny Bairstow is the next man.

OUT! A wicket against the run of play. Bishoo who was not bowling that well gets a wicket and a big one too. Root is walking back to the hut after getting another fifty-plus score. Bishoo floats a full ball on off and gets it to turn away from the batsman. Root tries to sweep it but it goes off the toe end to Blackwood at first slip who takes an easy catch. The free-flowing partnership between these two has been broken and Bishoo is delighted with the wicket. Half the side gone for England here!
Quicker on off, Root whips it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Tosses it up on off, Root lunges forward and blocks it.
Flatter on off, turning away. Root goes onto the back foot and defends it.
Drags his length back on middle, Stokes punches it through mid on for a run.
Lands it on a length outside off, Joe does not bother playing at it.
Back of a length on off, Root guides it to point.

Angles it into the pads, Stokes shuffles across and tries to flick but misses. The ball hits his thigh pad and rolls on the leg side behind the stumps. Root sets off for a leg bye. The keeper is quick to the ball and scores a direct hit at the striker's end but Joe has made his ground. A leg bye taken.
Back of a length on off, Stokes defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! He will punish you all day if you keep bowling that line and length. Full and wide outside off, Stokes leans into it and drives it through covers for another boundary.
Back of a length on middle, Stokes defends it off the back foot.

FOUR! A low full toss on middle, Root goes down on one knee and sweeps it behind square on the leg side for a boundary. The spinner is leaking a lot of runs here. 56 runs have been scored in the last 10 overs.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Floats it on middle, Root goes down on one knee and paddle sweeps it fine down the leg side for a couple.
Drags his length back on middle, Stokes camps back and drives it down to long on for a run.
Shorter in length outside off, Joe punches it through covers for a run.
Slower through the air around off, Root leaves it through to the keeper.
50-run stand up between Joe Root and Ben Stokes.

EDGY FOUR! Roach is deeply frustrated. He pitches it further up to the batsman outside off, induces an outside edge as Stokes attempts to drive. It screams through the vacant space between slips and gully for a boundary. Expensive over but you cannot blame the bowler for not trying. Roach is bowling his heart out, needs more support from his teammates.
Roach lands it on a length outside off, a bit on an inward movement, Stokes leans forward and across to whip it through mid-wicket but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Same area, off the front foot this time. The length is full to which Ben leans forward and drives for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Uses his height to good advantage! Stands tall inside the crease to a shortish ball and packs a punch through extra cover for a boundary.
Once again Stokes is solidly behind the line as he defends it to covers.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Stokes gets behind the line and defends it to the off side.

FOUR! The run-machine gets to another fifty. How costly will that drop catch prove? He was dropped on 8, if you remember. Tosses it up on off, Root gets down on one knee and sweeps it through mid-wicket and the ball races to the fence. His good run of form continues. He knows he still has a long way to go.
Joe Root has been in sublime form in the recent past. Hasn't looked troubled in this knock, apart from the dropped catch.
Floats it on off, Root punches it to covers.
Shorter in length, Root thinks about cutting it but then pulls out.
Drags his length back outside off, Root cuts it to point.
Plays it with the spin towards mid-wicket for a run.
Shorter outside off, Root punches it through covers for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! To add salt to the wound, Stokes drives this full toss outside off through covers for a boundary. Glorious!

DROPPED! FOUR! Another one goes down! These are regulation slip catches. Ben Stokes is the man who gets a life this time. Roach bowls it on a length on off from around the wicket. Stokes tries to defend it from the crease but gets an outside edge to Brathwaite at second slip. He does not pick it up and the ball hits his hands as it goes down to the third man fence for a boundary. The captain and the vice-captain both have got a reprieve each. Roach is frustrated as he lets out a loud roar in anguish.
A low full toss outside off, Stokes drives it straight to mid off.
Lands it on a length around off, Stokes gets it off the outer half to gully.
Time for Drinks.
Brings out the sweep shot through mid-wicket for a couple.
TURN! Slower through the air around off, Root prods forward to defend it but gets beaten by the away turn.
Tosses it up on off, Joe defends it off the front foot.
Drags his length back outside off, Root cuts it to point.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Flatter on off, Root punches it back to the bowler.
Good length outside off, Stokes shoulders his arms to it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.

Was there an edge? Full and wide outside off, Stokes goes for a drive away from the body but fails to middle it and it seems to have taken the edge as it goes through to the keeper. The players appeal but the umpire remains put. Also the Windies opt not to review it. The replays show that the bat had also hit the ground at the same time when the ball went past it. Had they reviewed it, the on-field called would have stayed as there would have been no conclusive evidence to overturn it. A very tough decision for the umpire, but a fair one in the end.
FOUR! Top shot! Full and wide outside off, Stokes goes down on one knee and clobbers it past mid off for a boundary. He really hits them hard.
Back of a length on off, Root punches it back past the bowler for a run.
Just ahead of a length on middle, Root drives it to mid on.
Kemar Roach is back into the attack. He was magnificent in his first spell and would look to make further inroads into the English batting lineup.
Half tracker outside off, Root punches it through covers for a run. Six short balls in the over, poor start from Bishoo.
Shorter in length again, Root punches it straight to covers.
Short on middle, Stokes punches it down to long on for a run.
On the shorter side again. Stokes rocks back and pulls it to mid-wicket.
Drags his length back outside off, Joe punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
FOUR! A loosener by Bishoo. Slower and shorter in length around middle. Root whips it through the vacant mid-wicket area for a boundary.
Devendra Bishoo comes into the attack. The leg spinner was not picked for the first Test. He would want to make an immediate impression here. A slip in place for him.
Lands it on a length, Stokes defends it watchfully.
Fuller on off, Stokes eases it to mid off. A good shot but for no runs.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Good bowling! Lands it on a length around middle. Nips away off the deck, squares Stokes up and takes his thigh pad as the ball goes on the bounce to second slip.
Wide! Well wide outside off again, Stokes does not fiddle with it. The umpire signals a wide.
Good length outside off, Stokes pokes at it and gets beaten.
Sprays it down the leg side this time. Stokes does not opt to play at it.
WIDE! Bowls a very full ball, way outside off, Stokes lets it through to the keeper.
FOUR! Crunched! Short on the stumps, sits up to be hit. Root swivels in his crease and pulls it behind square on the leg side for a boundary. He just loves playing from the back foot.
Fullish on off, Root eases it straight back down the ground. Gabriel in his followthrough does well to stop it.
Outswinger this time! Outside off on a length. Root lets it be.
Bowls it way down the leg side, Root lets it through to the keeper who dives to his left and collects the ball nicely.
Almost! The Windies' bowlers are getting good movement here. Fuller this time around off, gets it to seam into the batsman. Root tries to drive but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Brave leave! Good length outside off, nips back in off the deck. Root keeps his eyes on the ball and leaves it.
Lands it on a length outside off, Stokes shoulders his arms to it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

FOUR! Aerial but safe! Full on the pads, Stokes clips it over the mid-wicket fielder and the ball races to the fence. There were shouts of catch it but the fielder had no chance as that was timed really well.
Back of a length on leg stump, angling away. Stokes works it to mid-wicket.
Good length around off, Stokes lunges forward and defends it.
Lands it on that perfect length just outside off, Stokes does not bother playing at it.
Another full toss outside off, Root fails to pick it and hence does not connect with the drive. The ball goes along the ground to the keeper who makes a good stop.
Sprays it down the leg side, Root attempts the flick but misses.
FOUR! A gift for Joe Root. A low full toss outside off, Root leans into it and drives it through covers for a boundary. Replays show that Gabriel had overstepped but it was not called by the umpire.
Back of a length on off, Joe pushes it to mid off.
Lands it on a length outside off, Root opts not to play at it.
BEATEN! On a length around off, straightens a touch. Root tries to defend but gets beaten.
Lovely, lovely bowling from Holder! Bowls an away swinger this time which starts on middle and goes across the batsman. Stokes pokes at it and gets beaten.
Shorter in length outside off, Ben Stokes chops it to point.
Comes over the wicket and bowls it a touch fuller around off, gets some shape into the batsman. Stokes drives it hard back to the bowler.
Length ball outside off, Ben lets it be.
Back of a length, angling into the batsman. Stokes pushes it to mid on.
WIDE! Don't see that often. Bowls it very wide outside off, Stokes opts not to play at it and the umpire signals a wide.
Good length outside off, from around the wicket. Stokes does not fiddle with it.

There is a halt in play due to some sightscreen issue. It's just refusing to close and as a result the advertisement is still visible. One of the groundsmen is trying his best to fix the issue and after multiple attempts, it's done. Huge cheer from the crowd. Almost took 5 minutes there which will hurt the already hurt overrate.
Lands it on a length on off, Root defends it solidly.
Just ahead of a length around off, Root watchfully lets it through to the keeper.
A tad fuller on leg stump, Root tries to work it on the leg side but gets a soft leading edge towards mid off.
Even the full tosses are not being put away. Root tries to drive but gets a thick outside edge along the ground to second slip.
Sprays down the leg side, Root tries to flick but misses.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Good length around off, Stokes gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Ben Stokes strides out to the middle.

OUT! Dragged on! As Nasser Hussain on-air mentioned it has to be the perfect inswinger and he delivers one. Full ball around off, seaming back in. Malan goes for a drive but gets an inside edge onto the stumps. They were more on the back of a length side before lunch to Malan and it appears the bowling coach pointed that out to them. The fuller one has done the trick. Brilliant from Holder. An early wicket after the break, just what the visitors wanted. England are 4 down now.
Good length outside off, Malan shoulders his arms to it.
Inward movement this time. On a length on middle, Malan tucks it to mid-wicket.
Lands it on a length outside off, Malan first thinks about cutting it but then lets it through to the keeper.
Yorker! Another one, this time it is on off and bowled at 92 kmph. Root does well to jam it out.
Goes wide of the crease and bowls it on a length around off, Root lunges forward and defends it.
Tries to bowl a surprise yorker on the pads, Malan just gets his bat down in time and it goes off the toe-end to the fine leg fielder for a run.
Good length around middle and leg, Malan hops and defends it.
FOUR! Poor length! Short and wide outside off, just sits up for the batsman. Malan cuts it over point and into the fence for another boundary.
Back of a length on middle, Malan camps back and defends it.
Shannon Gabriel will bowl from the other end. He bowled really well in the first session.
Again fuller in length but way outside off, Root does not need to play at it.
A tad fuller on off, Root pushes it in the cover region for no run.
Lands it on a length outside off, Joe watchfully lets it through to the keeper.
Good length around off, swinging away from the batsman. Root is in no mood to play at it.
Back of a length on off, Root camps back and defends it.
Lands it on a length outside off, Root lets it be.

FOUR! NO BALL! Not the ideal start for the Windies here. Short and wide outside off, Root cuts it through point and the ball races to the fence. A real loosener by Holder. He has also overstepped there.
We're back for the second session. The players and the umpires are out in the middle. Joe Root and Dawid Malan will continue their innings. Jason Holder will continue after the break.
...Day 1, Session 2...

A session which the Windies will be mighty pleased with. Their bowlers were very accurate with their lines and lengths. They never let the Englishmen score freely and also chipped in with three very important wickets. It would have been an even better session had Powell not dropped the opposition skipper, Joe Root. He along with Malan will look to stitch a good partnership and take England out of trouble. The away side will want to continue picking wickets after the break. Join us for an action-packed second session in a while.
Flatter on off, turning away. Malan guides it to gully. LUNCH ON DAY 1!
Flicks it towards deep mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! EASY-PEASY! Loopy ball on off, Root leans into the drive and places it through mid off for a delightful boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted ball outside off, Root leans into it and drives it through covers. The fielder gives it a chase and does well to stop the ball inside the boundary. Two runs taken by the batsmen.
Tucks it to mid-wicket with the turn.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. Another maiden for Holder. England finding run-scoring really difficult here.
On a length outside off, Malan is in no mood to play at it.
Good length on middle, Malan works it to mid-wicket.
Lands it on a length on off, Dawid defends it watchfully.
Similar length ball on off this time, Malan gets a soft outside edge to gully.
Good length on off, angling away. Malan tries to defend it but gets beaten.
Gives it air on middle, Root plants his front foot ahead and works it to short mid-wicket with the turn.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Darts it on off, Root defends it watchfully.
Plays it with the spin through square leg and bags a couple.
Tosses it on off, Root lunges forward and defends it.
Flatter on off, turning back in. Joe defends it off the back foot.
Lands it on a length outside off, Malan lets it be. A maiden for Holder. The Windies are not giving England free runs here, something they were culprit of in the first Test match.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Back of a length on off, gets some extra bounce. Malan plays it with soft hands towards gully.
Good length outside off, Dawid plays inside the line and lets it through to the keeper.
Fuller in length on off, Malan defends it off the back foot.
Lands it on a length on middle, Malan defends it solidly.
Loopy ball outside off, Root gets it off the inner half towards the bowler.
FOUR! Fires in a full toss, seeing Root go down for the paddle sweep. Joe connects and plays it fine down the leg side and the ball races to the fence.
Flighted ball on middle, Root works it with the spin through mid-wicket for a couple.
Floats it on off, Malan eases it towards deep mid off for a run.
Plays it with the turn towards mid-wicket for a run.
Tosses up his first ball on off, spinning into the batsman. Root defends it off the front foot.
Roston Chase is into the attack. He had a good time with the ball in the last game, has a slip and short leg in place for him to start with.
Length ball outside off, Malan opts not to play at it.
Good length outside off, Malan lets it be.
Shorter in length on middle, Dawid tucks it to mid-wicket.
Back of a length on off, Malan camps back and defends it.
Bowls it on leg stump, Malan tucks it on the leg side.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Similar length outside off, Root this time does not play at it.

DROPPED! OH, NO, NO, NO! You just cannot drop Root and he won't give you an easier chance. Back of a length outside off, Root tries to force it through the off side but gets an outside edge to Powell at first slip who spills it. Root had started his walk back after he edged it. Gabriel can't believe it. Joe gets a reprieve. He would want to make them pay for it.
Shorter in length on off, Root pushes it towards mid off and shouts 'NOOO'.
A tad fuller outside off, Root does not fiddle with it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
WIDE! Bangs it in short down the leg side, also bounces above the batsman. Dowrich does well to dive to his left and collect it. The umpire signals a wide.
Back of a length on off, Root camps back and defends it to gully.
Length ball on middle, Malan defends it off the front foot with ease.
Bowls it outside off, Malan does not opt to play at it.
GOOD LEAVE! Lands it on a length just outside off, gets some inward movement. Malan watches the ball well and lets it through to the keeper.
Back of a length on off, Malan defends watchfully.
Length ball on off, Malan camps back and defends it.
Good length outside off, Malan shoulders his arms to it.
After an outstanding first spell by Kemar Roach, he has been given some rest. Jason Holder comes back into the attack.
Back of a length around off, Root guides it down towards third man for a couple.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Almost drags it on! Fullish on off, seaming back in. Root tries to drive it but gets an inside edge onto his pads. That was crashing onto the stumps but Root's pads saved him there.
Bowls it on a length outside off, comes in a little. Root watchfully lets it through to the keeper.
A tad fuller outside off, inviting Root to drive but Root lets it be.
Good length outside off, Root is in no mood to play at it.
A touch fuller on off, Root pushes it towards covers to keep strike.
Almost an edge! Root almost falling for the trap. Roach bowls a wide and short ball outside off, Root goes for the cut but gets beaten. That could so easily have taken the edge.
A tad shorter on off, Root defends it off the back foot.
Back of a length on off, Root camps back and defends it.
Fuller on off, Root eases it to mid off.
BEATEN! He is creating a lot of problems for the English batsmen. Lands it on a length around off, moves away from the batsman. Root pokes at it and gets beaten.
Lands it on a length outside off, Malan shoulders his arms to it.
Bangs it in short on middle, Dawid mistimes his pull through square leg for a couple.
Good length on middle, angling across. Malan gets an outside edge which goes on the bounce to third slip.
Back of a length on off, Malan defends it off the back foot.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Back of a length on off, Root gets a soft outside edge towards third slip who makes a half-stop and concedes a run.
Shannon Gabriel is back into the attack as well. Good move by Jason Holder, bringing his main pacer back and attacking the Englishmen.
Dawid Malan strides out to the middle.

OUT! Persisting with Kemar Roach has reaped rewards for the Windies here. This was probably the last ball of his long spell and he gets a wicket. He bowls a full ball outside off, nipping back in. Stoneman goes for the expansive cover drive but gets an inside edge to Dowrich who makes no mistake. The players appeal and the umpire gives it out. There was a clear edge there. Stoneman is walking back to the hut and England are in a spot of bother here. The visitors are ecstatic!
Angles it into the pads. Stoneman flicks it to mid-wicket.
Full and wide outside off, swinging away. Stoneman points his bat skywards and lets it through to the keeper.
Lands it on a length on middle, Stoneman defends it by covering the line of the ball.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Bangs it in short down the leg side. Stoneman lets it through to the keeper.
Full on middle, Stoneman clips it through mid-wicket. The fielder from mid on gives it a chase and pulls it back before the ball crosses the rope. Three runs taken by the batsmen.
A tad fuller outside off, Stoneman does not opt to play at it. The ball swings further away after crossing the batsman. Dowrich does well to dive to his left and stop it.
Pitches it on a length outside off, Stoneman watchfully lets it through to the keeper.
Good length outside off, Stoneman lets it be.
Length outside off, Stoneman shoulders his arms to it.

Lands it just ahead of a length on middle, comes back into the batsman and with some extra bounce. Stoneman tries to leave it but the ball hits him on the thigh pad and goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Good length outside off, Root lets it be.
FOUR! This was so pleasing to the eye! Fuller outside off, Root with his lazy approach, leans into it and drives it through covers for a boundary.
JAFFA! That was beautifully bowled. Roach bowls it from wide of the crease, on a length around off, angles it into the batsman and gets it to straighten. Root tries to defend but gets beaten.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Shorter in length on off, Root guides it towards gully.

Time for Drinks. A good first hour of play for the Windies. They have not let England score freely and have also taken two wickets. The hosts on the other hand will have to rebuild and hope their captain Joe Root and Stoneman build a good partnership.
Back of a length on middle, Stoneman defends it off the back foot.
Wide enough for the batsman to play at it.
Lands it on a length outside off, Mark shoulders his arms to it.

FOUR! That was in the air... but safe! Bowls it fuller outside off, Stoneman pushes at it and gets it off the outer half through backward point and the ball races to the fence. So easily could have been the third for the Windies.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Lands it on a length outside off, Stoneman shoulders his arms to it.
Jason Holder is into the attack. Three slips and a gully for him.
The batsman has driven it through mid off.
A well-directed bouncer by Roach to welcome Root. The English skipper does well to duck under it.
Joe Root, the skipper, strides out to the middle.

OUT! That was as plumb as you get! What a start for the Windies! Both the opening bowlers have one wicket each now. Roach goes wide of the crease and bowls a fast full ball on off, tailing back in. Westley tries to drive it but gets beaten and the ball hits him on the pads. The fielders go up in an appeal and the umpire rules it out. Westley straightaway starts walking back to the dressing room as he knew he was a dead duck. West Indies are off to a great start here and they would want to build on it.
Back of a length on off, Westley punches it through covers and the batsmen run two.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Lands it on a length outside off, Westley shoulders his arms to it. Kemar Roach is into his sixth over. A long spell for him.
Bowls it fuller on middle, Stoneman with minimal foot movement tries to drive it. The ball takes the the outer half and goes through covers for a couple.
Just ahead of a length on middle, Stoneman stays on the back foot and defends it towards mid on.
Length ball around off, angling across the batsman. Stoneman plays inside the line and lets it through to the keeper.
Bowls it on a length, jags back into the batsman. Westley gets it off the inner half towards fine leg for a run.
Lands it on a length outside off, Westley tries to defend it but gets beaten.

EDGED BUT SHORT! Gabriel is bowling testing lines here. Good length on off, nips away. Westley pokes at it and gets an outside edge which falls just short of Holder in the slip cordon. He does well to stop it though.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Bowls it on the pads, Stoneman works it to mid-wicket.
BEAUTY! Lands it on a length around off, gets it to straighten off the deck. Westley is opened up as he gets beaten on the outside edge.

LOVELY TIMING! Stoneman did not try to hit this too hard. A tad fuller on off, by Roach. Stoneman eases it through covers. The fielder from point gives it a chase and does well to keep it down to two.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Fuller on off, Stoneman plays it towards point.
Angles it into the pads, Westley tries to work it on the leg side but misses and the ball hits him on the thigh pad. End of a successful over.
Bangs in a bouncer on leg stump, Westley ducks under it.
Length on off, jagging back in. Tom tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads. He is bowling at a good pace here.
Good length on off, Westley defends it off the front foot.
Tom Westley is the next man in.

OUT! Gabriel gets the big fish! Cook who scored a double ton in the last game has to depart early. Shannon lands it on a length on middle, angling across the batsman. Cook pokes at it and gets an outside edge to Kyle Hope at third slip who takes an excellent catch diving forward to his right. A great return for Shannon Gabriel. He is all pumped up. An early wicket for the Windies, just what they wanted. Interestingly, this was the first ball Gabriel bowled to Cook today.

CLOSE SHAVE! Back of a length on middle, Stoneman tucks it towards mid-wicket and sets off for a run. Bishoo from mid on comes running in, picks it up cleanly and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. The batsmen complete a run. Had he hit, it would have been close.
Fullish on off, Cook eases it to mid off.
Angles it down the leg side from around the wicket. Cook misses the flick and the ball goes through to the keeper.
Fuller and outside off, Cook does not fiddle with it.
Just ahead of a length outside off, Cook shoulders his arms to it.
Good length on off, Cook prods forward and defends it.

FOUR! Cook plays this shot to great effect. He played it a lot of times in the last game and does it again. Length outside off, Cook plants his front foot forward and plays it with an angled bat past the diving third slip fielder and the ball races to the fence.
Bowls it down the leg side. Stoneman misses the flick and it is collected by Dowrich behind the stumps.
Good length on leg stump, jags back in a touch. Stoneman tries to clip it but gets hit high on the pads.
Lands it on a length around off, angling across the batsman. Stoneman plays inside the line and lets it through to the keeper.
On the shorter side on middle, Stoneman does well to evade it.
Sprays it on the pads, Mark works it down towards short fine leg for no runs.
Length on off, Stoneman tries to defend it but gets an inside edge onto his pads as the ball roll towards mid-wicket. He is playing a touch away from his body.
Fuller on middle, Cook lunges forward and defends it.
Good length outside off, Cook points his bat skywards and lets it through to the keeper.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

FOUR! Not a good follow-up delivery. A tad short and outside off. Cook cashes in on the width offered and punches it through backward point. The fielder gives it a chase and puts in a dive but fails to stop the ball from crossing the boundary.
LOVELY! Roach was their best bowler in the last game and he has started off well here. Bowls it from wide of the crease on off, gets it to straighten off the pitch. Cook pokes at it and gets beaten.
Good length outside off, from around the wicket. Cook defends it towards point.
Hits the good length area again around middle and off. Stoneman defends it solidly. A maiden by Gabriel, that should give him some confidence.
Short of a length on middle, Mark camps back and defends it.
Bowls it from wide of the crease. Lands it on a length, angling across. Stoneman defends it towards point.
A touch fuller on off, Stoneman pushes it towards mid off.
Fuller on off, Stoneman defends it by covering the line of the ball. A good start to this over by Gabriel.
Back of a length, angling across the batsman. Stoneman plays inside the line and lets it through to the keeper.
Lands it on a length outside off, Cook lets it through to the keeper.
Full and wide outside off, Cook does not fiddle with it.
Good length on off, Cook defends it towards mid off.
Comes over the wicket to Stoneman and bangs it in short, aimed at his rib cage. Mark tucks it towards square leg and takes a run. That was nicely played by him.
Bowls it from closer to the stumps on a length around off, Cook pushes it towards cover-point for a run.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
The West Indian players are wearing black armbands mourning the death of their bowling coach's mother.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Just ahead of a length on middle, Mark drives it to mid on with not a lot of foot movement.
Fuller outside off, Stoneman leans into it and drives it through covers for a couple.

EDGY FOUR! Stoneman is off the mark. Not in convincing fashion but he won't mind. Gabriel lands it on a length on off, nips away off the deck. Stoneman tries to defend it with soft hands but gets an outside edge past the diving third slip fielder and to the boundary.
Length ball outside off, Stoneman shoulders his arms to it.
Almost similar to a delivery Kemar Roach bowled in the first over of the last game. Full and very wide outside off. Stoneman lets it through to the keeper who collects it in front of second slip.
Shannon Gabriel will bowl from the other end. He will be coming up the hill. He has three slips and a gully in place for him. The Windies will also hope that he has sorted his no ball issues.
Good length on off, Cook defends it solidly. A good first over from Roach. He has hit good lines and lengths by cutting down his pace a little.
BEATEN! That was fast from Roach. Full and outside off, inviting Cook for the drive. Alastair obliges and goes for it but gets beaten.
A touch fuller outside off, Cook points his bat skywards and lets it through to the keeper.
Good length on off, Cook defends it watchfully.
First runs of the Test match! Very full and wide outside off, Cook jams it through backward point for a couple.
No looseners! Right on the money. Comes steaming in, lands it on a length on off. Cook lunges forward and like always defends it solidly.

The players and the umpires are out in the middle and we are all set for the action to get underway. The solid Alastair Cook and Mark Stoneman will open the batting for England. The pacey Kemar Roach will open the bowling for West Indies. He has three slips and a gully in place for him.
TOSS - England win their second toss in a row and they opt to bat. Two changes for the Windies. Shannon Gabriel and Devendra Bishoo come in for Miguel Cummins and Alzarri Joseph.

Hello and welcome to the first day of the second Test between England and West Indies at Headingley. A very lopsided first game meant that the hosts have taken a 1-0 lead. They dominated the visitors in every department and Root would hope for the same to continue. The skipper has already confirmed his eleven with one change that is Chris Woakes coming in for the outgoing Toby Roland-Jones. The Windies on the other hand, would want to put their defeat behind and come out with new plans. They will have to play out of their skins, if they are to surge a comeback in this series. Let us hope we witness an even contest between bat and ball. Stay tuned for the all-important toss in a while.
